findTerms.title: Find terms
findTerms.intro: Proposes the concepts a document or table defines and uses: business concepts, roles, organization types, policies, processes and regulations, never named people or companies. Every proposal lands in the review queue as a draft, with the passages it came from.
findTerms.documentHelp: The reference library documents you may read.
findTerms.noDocuments: The reference library holds no document you may read yet.
findTerms.fileHelp: PDF, Word, Markdown, HTML, eCFR XML or plain text.
findTerms.urlHelp: A web page or document served over http or https, fetched once.
findTerms.newDocumentNote: A new document joins the reference library as proposed, in the domains below, until someone keeps or discards it. A document already in the library is not added again: the scan reads the library's copy.
findTerms.tableDomainHelp: The domain of the table to read.
findTerms.tableHelp: A registered table that holds definitions or documentation, such as a data dictionary, policy text kept as rows or knowledge-base articles.
findTerms.termColumnHelp: The column holding each row's term.
findTerms.definitionColumnHelp: The column holding the term's definition. Each row is offered for review as a term with this definition.
findTerms.idColumnHelp: The column that identifies a row. Every proposal cites the rows it came from by this value.
findTerms.textColumnHelp: The column holding each row's text, which the AI model reads for the terms it defines.
findTerms.tableNote: The rows are read as your role reads them: its row rules and masks apply. A table scan adds nothing to the reference library.
findTerms.domainsHelp: The domains you are working in. The new terms are placed in them, and a new document is added to the library with them.
findTerms.chooseTable: Choose a table, its ID column and its text column.
findTerms.chooseTerms: Choose a table, its term column and its definition column.
findTerms.budgetNote: The scan uses the organization's AI model and counts against your role's AI budget.
findTerms.termsNote: No AI model reads the rows, so nothing counts against your role's AI budget.
findTerms.rescanHint: Scan the document's current content again. The new scan shows the terms the ontology does not hold yet and those that match its terms; earlier decisions stand.
findTerms.rescanTableHint: Read the table's rows again and scan them. The new scan shows the terms the ontology does not hold yet and those that match its terms; earlier decisions stand.
findTerms.removedDocumentHint: This document was removed from the reference library. Its citations are kept as they were quoted.
findTerms.tableScanHint: Read from the table {{domain}}.{{table}}: each row's {{text_column}}, cited by its {{id_column}}.
findTerms.tableTermsHint: Read from the table {{domain}}.{{table}}: each row's {{term_column}} with its {{definition_column}}.
findTerms.progressMerging: Merging what was found into candidate terms...
findTerms.budgetLimited: The role's AI budget held a call to {{tokens}} output tokens, so an answer may be cut short.
findTerms.leftOut: Left out: {{count}} not ontology concepts (such as named people or companies), {{misquoted}} not quoted from their passage, {{unresolved}} not resolved into a term.
findTerms.acceptSelectedHint: Each selected draft is decided as it proposes: a new term is added, a match is merged into the term it matches.
findTerms.proposeRelationshipsHint: Runs Generate with AI, Relationships over the ontology, now including the terms accepted here.
findTerms.homonyms: The same word with another meaning: {{names}}
findTerms.definitionSynthesizedHint: No passage defines it outright; this definition is drawn from the passages marked as used.
findTerms.synonymsHelp: The names kept here are added as synonyms of the term.
findTerms.conflictsHint: These passages cannot both be true, so they are shown side by side.
findTerms.useDefinition: Use this definition for the term
findTerms.name: Name
